name: Costa Brava Holm Oak Forest
description: Mediterranean holm oak forest: 11 agents from the mycorrhizal network (keystone) to raptors and the coastal tourism economy; Fire & Microclimate Regulation degrades exponentially past the threshold, and three edges into Understory & Matorral are rescaled to the in-degree cap (Step 3.8). Small losses are priced linearly (damage model area_loss, Step 8d.1). Illustrative. Derivations: gaia/cases/definitions/CASE_NOTES.md.

units_per_ha.note: Chosen so the per-tree absorption gives ~1.8 t CO2/ha/yr.

unit_value.source: owner specification (case docstring), no external source
unit_value.note: Revenue per holm oak felled (one-off). Rated Medium in the case docstring, but no market source is cited.

safe_threshold_ratio.source: owner specification (case docstring), no external source
safe_threshold_ratio.note: Safe extraction threshold, lower than temperate forest for drought and fire (stated rationale, no cited source); under the area_loss damage model (Step 8d.1) the depletion beyond which the REMAINING resource starts to degrade; below it each hectare lost costs its average value.

agent[*].dependency_weight.source: owner specification (case docstring), no external source
agent[*].dependency_weight.note: Rated Medium in the case docstring; an expert judgement with no cited source.

annual_value_per_ha.source: de Groot et al. (2012), Ecosystem Services 1:50-61: woodlands Int$1,588/ha/yr; minus climate regulation Int$7 (SM Table 9.1)
annual_value_per_ha.note: Every agent; the dependency weights split it. Figure partly from memory, to be checked against the paper (Step 8); 2007 Int$ used as € with no currency or price-year conversion; a global woodland mean, not a Mediterranean holm-oak valuation.

steepness.note: Degradation of the REMAINING resource past the safe threshold (damage model area_loss, Step 8d.1, as for Posidonia): zero up to the threshold, then a logistic with its inflection 15% into the post-threshold span, the same curve for every agent except Fire & Microclimate Regulation. The damage of each agent is D + (1 - D) x degradation, so its slope at small losses is exactly 1 (each hectare lost costs its average value) and the curve shapes only the threshold behaviour. Not fitted to field data (calibration regime B).

base.note: Degradation of Fire & Microclimate Regulation past the safe threshold (area_loss, Step 8d.1): zero up to the threshold, then exponential over the post-threshold span (fire feedback, no plateau): (base^((D - t)/(1 - t)) - 1)/(base - 1); not fitted to fire data.

agents.name: Mycorrhizal Fungi
agents.description: Keystone underground network — nutrient/water transport, cascades to all tree regeneration

agents.name: Soil Microbiome
agents.description: Soil microbiome and biocrusts — nitrogen fixation, nutrient cycling, erosion prevention

agents.name: Canopy Trees
agents.description: Remaining canopy trees — self-reinforcing decline from microclimate loss and network fragmentation

agents.name: Understory & Matorral
agents.description: Understory shrubs and aromatic plants — microclimate collapse and biodiversity loss

agents.name: Pollinators & Insects
agents.description: Keystone pollination services — base of animal food web, agricultural crop dependency

agents.name: Forest Birds
agents.description: Nesting and migratory stopover habitat — seed dispersal, insect control, ecotourism

agents.name: Forest Mammals
agents.description: Habitat displacement — predator-prey disruption, human-wildlife conflict, crop damage

agents.name: Raptors & Apex Predators
agents.description: Apex trophic control — carrion processing, extreme K-strategy vulnerability, trophic cascade trigger

agents.name: Watershed & Water Cycle
agents.description: Aquifer recharge, flood control, drought buffering — Costa Brava water and tourism supply

agents.name: Fire & Microclimate Regulation
agents.description: Fire risk amplification, loss of shade and moisture buffering — self-reinforcing, no plateau

agents.name: Human Communities
agents.description: Water, fire protection, tourism economy, traditional livelihoods — Costa Brava coastal dependency
